To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
‘The polarization of the Crab nebula has a remarkable organization on a scale of about 10 arc seconds, with no evidence for small-scale structure on a scale of 1.6 arc s.’
we have mapped the linear polarization of the optical emission from the Crab Nebula with an unprecedented resolution and signal-to-noise.

the polarization structure of the Crab Nebular is dominated by the large-scale structure, but the small-scale structure is not negligible and is important in understanding energy transport mechanisms and the connection between polarization features and filamentary structure.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the new CCD technology has made possible a new era in the study of the Crab Nebular magnetic field.
CCD imaging/spectropolariometry is a powerful technique for studying the structure of the magnetic fields in astrophysical objects.

the new CCD camera can be used for polarization measurements with a resolution of 1–2 arc s and a signal-to-noise of 10–100 per polarization measurement, which is an order of magnitude improvement over the best photographic and photoelectric work.
